description:
observerEci computes the observer's geocentric ECI position on a spherical Earth (RE=6378.137) instead of the WGS84 ellipsoid. The parallax correction in equatorialToHorizontal uses a fixed equatorial radius (6378.137/149597870.7 AU) instead of the observer's true geocentric distance, though that error is sub-arcsecond for planets and ~0.01° for the Moon.

Expected: observerEci places the observer on the WGS84 ellipsoid surface (height=0) using the prime-vertical radius of curvature. The z-component uses N·(1−e²)·sin(φ), not RE·sin(φ). At φ=45° the x-y radial magnitude changes by ~7.6 km and z shifts by ~−22.7 km relative to the spherical model.

Acceptance criteria:
- observerEci(φ=0°) produces magnitude = WGS84 semi-major axis (6378.137 km) exactly, with z=0. [repo-data: WGS84 definition: a=6378137m is the equatorial radius — a point on the equator must sit at radius a]
- observerEci(φ=π/2) produces magnitude = WGS84 polar radius b=a·(1−f)=6356.752 km, with x=y=0. [reporter: The prior commit a5cf0981f on main already implements this test]
- observerEci uses N=a/√(1−e²·sin²φ) for the prime-vertical radius and N·(1−e²)·sin(φ) for the z-component, not RE·sin(φ). Verified numerically at φ=π/4: x-y radial magnitude = N·cos(φ) ≈ 4517.6 km (sphere gives 4510.0 km, diff ~7.6 km); z = N·(1−e²)·sin(φ) ≈ 4487.3 km (sphere gives 4510.0 km, diff ~−22.7 km). [code-invariant: WGS84 ellipsoid formula: z = N·(1−e²)·sin(φ); the sphere formula z = RE·sin(φ) is structurally wrong]

Domain facts:
- WGS84 ellipsoid: a = 6378137.0 m (6378.137 km), f = 1/298.257223563, e² = 2f − f² ≈ 0.00669438.
- Prime-vertical radius: N(φ) = a / √(1 − e²·sin²φ).
- ECEF at geodetic (φ, λ, h=0): (N·cosφ·cosλ, N·cosφ·sinλ, N·(1−e²)·sinφ).
- ECI = Rz(GMST)·ECEF, where GMST is the Greenwich Mean Sidereal Time at the given JD.
- At φ=45°, N ≈ 6388.9 km; the x-y radial magnitude is N·cos(45°) ≈ 4517.6 km (sphere: 4510.0 km, diff +7.6 km); z is N·(1−e²)·sin(45°) ≈ 4487.3 km (sphere: 4510.0 km, diff −22.7 km). The '~11 km x/y, ~2 km z' in the prior domain facts were incorrect — the z error at mid-latitudes is ~23 km, similar in magnitude to the polar error (~21 km).
